sections.content: How many people are "authors, writers and translators"?

70,220 people

were counted on the census as "authors, writers and translators" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Authors, writers and translators write, edit and evaluate literary material for publication, including scripts and narrative for film, TV, radio and computer games and animations; and translate spoken and written statements into different languages. This category does not include writing for newspapers, magazines and other periodicals.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "authors, writers and translators", 11.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "authors, writers and translators" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "authors, writers and translators" included:

  • artists
  • biological scientists
  • publicans and managers of licensed premises

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "authors, writers and translators" there were more women than men (60% compared with 40%).

This means "authors, writers and translators" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "culture, media and sports occupations".

Men made up 40% and women made up 60% of "authors, writers and translators"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "authors, writers and translators" included:

  • bed and breakfast and guest house owners and proprietors
  • market research interviewers
  • optometrists

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "authors, writers and translators" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "authors, writers and translators" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "authors, writers and translators", 15.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (52.3% compared with 47.7%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (67.8%) than an employee (32.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Hackney, this is in the same region of London.
